To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
successive discriminative responding is governed by several stimulus controls, including delayed control by a transition in component variable-interval schedule.

the power-function exponent relating ratios of responses to ratios of reinforcer deliveries decreases systematically with time since component transition, and this reduction is independent of the absolute rate of reinforcer delivery.

(a) the power function relating responses in successive components to the ratio of reinforcers in the components provides a measure of stimulus discrimination that is independent of the absolute rate of response reinforcement, and (b) this measure of stimulus control decreases systematically with increasing time after component transition.

the development of a model of the temporal organization of operant behavior.
the nature of the stimulus control of successive discriminations.

the results of the experiments support the hypothesis that component transition is a relational basis for the discrimination of stimuli in a successive discrimination.

the present experiments provide evidence that the component-transition effect is an instance of action-at-a-temporal distance, in which a change in the environment at one time is followed by a change in the organism at a later time, and that this effect is a component of stimulus control in the sense of the stimulus-response theory of discrimination.
component transition is the basis for the discrimination, and that the discrimination is maintained by the reinforcement contingencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the component transition is the relational basis for the successive discrimination.
component transition is a stimulus for the discriminative response.
the component transition, which is a temporal relation among events, is an important stimulus controlling discriminative behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the component transition is a stimulus that can be learned to control behavior.
the component transition is a stimulus that can exert control over the organism's behavior.
the stimulus properties of the environment are not limited to the immediate environment, but extend to the past and future, and that these past and future properties can influence behavior.
